For every real number δ with 0 < δ < 1, there exists a natural number d₀, depending only on δ, such that the following holds for every natural number d ≥ d₀, every real number κ satisfying 2 ≤ κ ≤ d^(1 − δ), and every natural number q satisfying q ≤ (δ/256)√κ log d. Natural numbers include zero, and d and q in these real expressions are cast to the reals.

Set n = 2q + 1. For each i ∈ Fin d, identified with its integer value i = 0, …, d − 1, define θᵢ = (i + 1/2)π/d and λᵢ = (κ + 1)/2 + ((κ − 1)/2) cos θᵢ. Let Λ be the real d by d diagonal matrix with diagonal entries λᵢ, and let μ = multivariateGaussian(0, Λ⁻¹) on d-dimensional real Euclidean space. Here the inverse and Gaussian measure have exactly the supplied standard totalized meanings: the Gaussian is obtained from the standard Gaussian by the affine map whose linear part is CFC.sqrt(Λ⁻¹).

For x in that Euclidean space, with ordinary coordinates xᵢ, set Q(x) = ∑ᵢ cos(nθᵢ)xᵢ². Define M = ∫ ‖x‖² dμ(x), b = ∫ Q(x) dμ(x), β = |b|/M, and B = (1 − exp(−4)) exp(−3). The norm is the full Euclidean norm, and the integrals are the real Bochner integrals with the supplied totalized conventions. Then all five assertions hold:
M > 0,
β > 0,
d/(2√κ) ≤ M,
d^((1 + δ)/2)/2 ≤ M,
and (B²/2)√d ≤ Mβ².
All displayed divisions, logarithms, square roots, real powers, and arithmetic use the supplied real conventions; n in cos(nθᵢ) is cast to the reals.
